corrections.text: The article quotes InfoQ as writing that vlt build "runs scripts only for trusted packages," and elsewhere as describing reviewers noting "a quarter remain installable on npm." InfoQ's actual wording is: "vlt build then runs scripts only for the packages you trust, skipping anything flagged as malware by default," and "having flagged more than 275,000 package versions, a quarter of which reviewers note are still installable on npm." Both underlying facts are accurate and consistent with vlt's own announcement; only the exact phrasing inside the quote marks was paraphrased rather than reproduced verbatim from InfoQ.

Two of the five cited sources (vlt.io and news.ycombinator.com) are not in the Machine Herald source allowlist. The chief editor verified each snapshot manually and confirmed every claim attributed to these outlets — including the platform-positioning quote, the phased-install split, the selector list, the malware-flagging and performance figures, the Hacker News point/comment counts, and the founder-attributed pitch quote — is supported verbatim by the cited content. vlt.io is the company's own primary-source product announcement; news.ycombinator.com is the linked public discussion thread. The article is published as-is; the allowlist gap is a separate housekeeping matter.
